subsystems.known_behavior: ATSAMD51J19A confirmed by board inspection. Full clock-tree/analog-block bring-up (MCLK/GCLK/OSCCTRL/OSC32KCTRL/SUPC/NVMCTRL/CMCC/AC/ADC0/ADC1/DAC/USB) traced instruction-by-instruction and concretely reproduced Reset_Handler through steady-state main loop.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Standard Microchip/ASF4/CMSIS SAMD51 clock-init sequence; no vendor-secret behavior. Implementable cleanly, not a binary-compatibility concern.

subsystems.known_behavior: FUN_00006968 ("homing", analyst label) runs before the radio probe; gated on a GPIO hold (PA22) with a real timeout exit; PA22 is later reused for the unrelated "hold to save" path.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Replacement firmware needs a product decision on whether/how to reproduce a boot-time wait-for-signal step at all.
subsystems.missing_fact: physical identity/purpose of the PA22 signal this boot-time routine waits on is explicitly undocumented ("no physical function claimed")

subsystems.known_behavior: TC0-TC3 in CC0/period-match mode drive an ISR chain into a GPIO OUTSET/OUTCLR pulse (FUN_00005898/0xd388); confirmed pin map TC0->PB10, TC1->PA08, TC2->PB12, TC3->PA10. Semantic passes additionally resolved the pinMode primitive (0xd300) and a paired stepper-driver enable/disable GPIO sequence (0x77a0 enable; 0x77f8/0x7868 disable).
subsystems.implementation_requirements: The step-pulse mechanism (timer-match ISR toggling a GPIO) is a standard, cleanly-replaceable pattern; replacement need not bit-match vendor timer register values, only reproduce STEP pulse timing/electrical behavior on the same physical pins.
subsystems.missing_fact: exact fixed-point ramp/rate coefficients and acceleration-curve formula used by the rate/phase machinery (FUN_00006338/0x5274/0x6e68) have not been decompiled to formula level

subsystems.known_behavior: Direction is carried as a sign bit through the step-delta/move-distance computation feeding the GPIO pulse mechanism; the manual documents a configurable A/B orientation invert. XLR-4 output is a bipolar winding drive (A+/A-/B+/B-), i.e. the onboard driver ICs convert an MCU-side STEP+DIR-like control into winding current themselves.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Need the actual DIR GPIO pin(s)/register(s) per channel to reproduce direction behavior electrically.
subsystems.missing_fact: which GPIO pin(s) carry the per-channel DIR signal to the onboard stepper-driver ICs are not identified in current evidence

subsystems.known_behavior: AUTOPILOT_LIVE_POSITION[channel] (0x20002064+channel*4) is the single live-position store, execution-confirmed as the exact value the I command returns and G's distance computation consumes.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Straightforward per-channel signed-integer position counter; no ambiguity for replacement.

subsystems.known_behavior: Phase/velocity state machine (0x6338) gated on 0x20001b14[channel], move-commit threshold (|distance|>8) in FUN_00006fd8, busy-gate reader (0x5ee8), target-reached completion (0x5958). Semantic passes additionally resolved the per-channel move/ramp-profile initializer (0x6e68) and its record-reversal counterpart (0x4ae4), both keyed on the same 0x120-byte-stride per-channel-per-mode config struct motor-config-persistence.md already documents byte-for-byte.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Replacement can implement its own ramp/acceleration algorithm against the same struct layout and move-commit contract (threshold, busy gate, phase state machine shape) without needing the vendor's exact arithmetic.
subsystems.missing_fact: exact fixed-point ramp/rate coefficients (same gap as STEP generation, above) — not required to reproduce observable behavior, only to bit-match vendor motion profiles

subsystems.known_behavior: Newly resolved this session (Pass 6, bounded decompile): 0x77a0 asserts 2 driver-enable pins HIGH, delays 50ms, then pinMode(OUTPUT)s 8 STEP/DIR-family pins for the channel-0/1 driver chip; 0x77f8/0x7868 are the structural inverse (tri-state the 8 pins, reset-pulse the 2 enable pins). Not yet folded into docs/investigations/.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Replacement needs the real enable-pin power-up delay (50ms, confirmed) reproduced for driver-chip compatibility; the 8-pin OUTPUT/tri-state pattern is a safe default to replicate.
subsystems.missing_fact: exact GPIO pin identities (not just the structural pattern) driven by these enable/disable sequences are not resolved to concrete port/pin letters — the DAT_ globals feeding them were not traced to real addresses this pass

subsystems.known_behavior: User-manual-only: connecting an external controller (Dragonframe DMC-32, MRMC Ulti/Quad/Octo-Box) via one of the four RJ45 jacks disables/grays out Auto Mode while Manual Mode remains available; the Remote shows a source label ("MRMC inputs"/"DMC32 inputs"). RJ45 pinout for MRMC-style controllers is documented (pins: GND, 5V, STEP, DIR); Dragonframe DMC-32 uses a different assignment (manual page 25, not transcribed here).
subsystems.implementation_requirements: This is a whole external-interface product feature (external-controller presence detection, external STEP pulse counting/passthrough, Auto-Mode lockout) with zero firmware-side trace found anywhere in current evidence.
subsystems.missing_fact: no firmware code path has been traced for reading the RJ45 external STEP/DIR input pins or for detecting external-controller presence — the entire mechanism is undocumented on the firmware side

subsystems.known_behavior: Fully decoded binary 0xF0/0xE0 wire frame family, sent once per UI tick from a real quadrature-encoder-driven jog loop, received by the AutoPilot's dispatcher before any ASCII command. Gap Resolution A/B (this session, tools/unicorn/virtual_link.py's `manual-f0e0` scenario) closed the remaining open items by disassembling ascii_dispatcher__CUSTOM's (0x8258) own 0xF0/0xE0 arms and concretely delivering representative frames: 0xE0's per-record field layout is BYTE-IDENTICAL to 0xF0's (channel nibble @ byte6, sign+23-bit magnitude @ bytes 7-9) -- confirmed by delivering byte-identical record payloads under each marker and observing identical (channel, value) decode into FUN_00005448/FUN_00005274. 0xE0's only real difference is a per-channel latch/cache (0x20001fdd/0x20001fe4/0x20001ff4) that suppresses a REPEAT at-limit (FUN_00005274, mode=4) call once a channel is already latched -- concretely demonstrated: an identical over-threshold 0xE0 record reaches FUN_00005274 on a cold delivery but is silently skipped once the latch is pre-set, while 0xF0 (no latch) re-fires unconditionally every delivery. No dead-man/timeout exists in current evidence: the latch's own timestamp field is written but has zero consumers anywhere in the image per the existing cached xref data -- motion is not automatically stopped or decayed when frames stop arriving; the RX-driven handler simply does not run again until another frame is delivered.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Wire grammar and field layout are fully specifiable for both 0xF0 and 0xE0 now. Replacement should decide (product choice, not an evidence gap) whether to reproduce the absence of a dead-man timeout or add one, since none is confirmed to exist in the vendor firmware.

subsystems.known_behavior: Segment model (points A-D, up to 3 segments, duration/ramp/delay/loop parameters) confirmed on-screen and in the wire schema. Two distinct populate-a-target paths exist: interactive confirm screens (mode 0/0x14, does NOT persist a live target) vs. the boot/reconnect bulk-push (mode 0x62, DOES persist and is concretely confirmed end-to-end through a real G-driven move-commit). Gap Resolution A (this session, tools/unicorn/virtual_link.py's `plus-interactive` scenario) closed the remaining CONCRETE gap: entering directly at the real AutoPilot dispatcher boundary (the same technique already used for the bulk-push leg, sidestepping the separately-documented cold-boot delivery blocker) with a real Remote-built interactive-mode ('+' mode=0x00, screen-5 site A/B) frame confirms, by execution, that the wire-supplied delta IS written into the per-channel record but target/dirty-flag stay at their pre-command state -- the interactive path cannot arm or commit a move by itself, exactly as the '>50' threshold documentation predicted, now proven rather than only disassembled.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: The full arm/no-arm contract is now proven both ways: replacement can implement its own confirm-and-arm mechanism around the bulk-push (mode 0x62) path and treat interactive confirms as record-only writes.
subsystems.missing_fact: which exact Remote UI row/highlight is shown at the moment call sites C/D (screens 9/10) send '+' remains PROBABLE, not CONFIRMED (an arithmetic extrapolation from other screens' own row-indexed calls, not directly observed for screens 9/10) -- a cosmetic UI-labeling question, not a behavioral one; see action-command-map.md Part 5 item 2

subsystems.known_behavior: Per-channel, per-mode target/position struct at 0x20001b40 (4 channels x 0x120 bytes) is documented byte-for-byte, including the mode-0 vs mode-N field offsets and the blank-default (target=0 or -1) provisioning gap. The interactive-vs-bulk-push arm/no-arm contract (see Auto Mode, above) is now concretely confirmed both ways.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Struct layout is a firmware-internal implementation detail replacement firmware need not match; the observable contract (persist -> G resolves target -> distance -> move-commit) is what must be reproduced, and is now fully specifiable.

subsystems.known_behavior: MC<0-3>/MC4 wire commands and their exact RAM write targets (0x2000006c/0x200000dc/0x200000f0/0x20000138 per channel) are confirmed; field 4 ("RETURN SPEED" on the Remote) is known to be used as a secondary-table index on the AutoPilot side, not a direct speed value.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: The wire schema and unlock semantics (MC4 clearing the boot-loop gate) are solid enough to reproduce directly.
subsystems.missing_fact: how the 4 MC-command fields (current, steps/s max, microstepping, return speed) are actually consumed by the motor driver beyond field 4's table-index use is unconfirmed -- "remains PROBABLE, not proven" per current evidence

subsystems.known_behavior: AutoPilot-initiated (not Remote-menu-initiated): four real GPIO motor-connector-presence probes build an MT frame, sent exactly once per boot; Remote reacts by opening the Choose-Type screen; MC4 (Continue) is the sole, concretely-confirmed condition that clears 0x20000060 and lets the AutoPilot's setup() loop exit into normal runtime.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Fully specifiable end-to-end contract for replacement: connector-presence probe -> MT -> Choose-Type UI -> MC4 -> unlock.

subsystems.known_behavior: Config blob at flash 0x12000 (4097 bytes), loaded to RAM at boot, dirty-flag/save-on-change mechanism, NVMCTRL.PARAM-derived page size (PSZ=6, 512B pages for the real ATSAMD51J19A), save triggers (PA22 hold >1000 ticks, or 20000-tick elapsed check). Entire round trip -- command in, dirty, save, real NVM erase+write, reboot recovery -- concretely demonstrated register-by-register.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Fully specifiable: page size/count derived from the real, physically-confirmed part; replacement can use its own flash-management code against the same logical layout or a clean-room equivalent.

subsystems.known_behavior: No debounce/latch on the digital arm; a bouncy insertion can produce multiple accepted config-reloads. Fully characterized bug, reproduced three independent ways; a software mitigation (consecutive-sample debounce) is designed and Unicorn-prototyped.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Replacement firmware is free to implement proper debounce from the start -- this subsystem's gap for vendor compatibility is fully understood, and for a clean-room replacement the fix is a known, designed pattern already prototyped in this project.

subsystems.known_behavior: Analog arm samples PB05 via ADC1 through an exponentially-smoothed filter (0x42a4, resolved this session) whose blend coefficient is permanently zero and whose one-shot latch never clears -- the very first (boot-time) sample is permanently latched for the whole power cycle, explaining the manual's "connect before power-up = noise baseline / less sensitive" behavior precisely.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Mechanism and its product-visible consequence are both fully understood; replacement can choose to reproduce this exact quirk or design a proper continuously-resampled filter instead (product decision, not an evidence gap).

subsystems.known_behavior: Core protocol pipeline milestone is CLOSED at the concrete evidence tier: real dispatcher structure, ASCII-vs-binary-frame discrimination (0xF0/0xE0 checked before any ASCII branch), and field parsing all traced and reproduced.
evidence_refs: docs/project-status.md (Current milestone: the core protocol pipeline)
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Dispatcher structure is fully specifiable for a from-scratch RX parser.

subsystems.known_behavior: Pending-event-counter array (one byte per event ID at 0x200025bc+event_id) and outbound dispatcher (0x9268) fully documented; 10 of 18 event slots have confirmed producers, the other 7 (events 2,3,8,9,11,12,14) have no found producer and are not currently observable product behavior.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Replacement only needs to reproduce the 10 events with confirmed real behavior; the 7 dormant slots are not required for observable-behavior compatibility.

subsystems.known_behavior: G, S, !0/!1, and I<channel><mode> are all execution-confirmed end-to-end (both firmwares, full round trip via tools/unicorn/virtual_link.py). '+' is confirmed for its wire schema and both real AutoPilot-side consequences: the bulk-push path (mode 0x62) computes+persists a live target end-to-end through a real move-commit, and the interactive path (mode 0x00, this session's Gap Resolution A) writes the record but concretely does NOT compute a target or dirty the buffer.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: G/S/!/I/+ are all ready to specify as-is, including both of '+' 's real, distinct behaviors (interactive record-write vs. bulk-push arm-and-persist).

subsystems.known_behavior: SERCOM2 in SPI Master mode, chip-select PA15, zero DMA, driven through a real Stream-derived C++ driver object -- CONFIRMED at the MCU-peripheral level. The external chip's exact identity is only PROBABLE from firmware register-pattern matching (SX127x/RFM9x-style), but hardware-reference.md's physical board inspection independently names the actual part: an Ai-Thinker Ra-01H module (a well-documented, commodity SX1276-based module).
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Replacement can target the Ra-01H/SX1276 directly via its public datasheet rather than needing byte-exact vendor-driver RE, closing the firmware-only PROBABLE gap with an independent hardware fact.
subsystems.missing_fact: the over-the-air RF-layer framing/modulation parameters used between Remote and AutoPilot on top of the SX1276 (vs. raw byte passthrough) are not established from current evidence

subsystems.known_behavior: USB-C is used only for firmware updates via the vendor's stock BOSSA-compatible SAM-D UART bootloader (VID 0x239A, standard 1200-baud touch-reset entry), occupying the first 16KB of flash (0x0000-0x3FFF) -- entirely separate from, and untouched by, the application image this project reverse-engineers.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: Replacement application firmware can be flashed via the existing standard bootloader unchanged, or updated with a modern equivalent; no RE-dependent behavior here.

subsystems.known_behavior: Confirmed to physically exist on the AutoPilot's input panel (board inspection); no firmware-side investigation exists.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: A real, user-visible status indicator; needs its own driving GPIO and pattern semantics before a replacement can reproduce it.
subsystems.missing_fact: no firmware investigation has traced which GPIO drives the status LED or what its blink/color/state patterns mean

subsystems.subsystem: error/failure behavior that matters to compatibility
subsystems.known_behavior: Specific, incidentally-discovered failure paths are documented: radio-probe failure -> real infinite retry with status print; NVM erase stall if PARAM/DONE bits are unmodeled; I9| silent out-of-bounds dead end with client-side timeout; digital trigger bounce risk. No systematic sweep of error/failure behavior exists beyond these.
subsystems.implementation_requirements: For a clean-room replacement, most of these are not behaviors worth bit-matching (e.g. the I9| dead end is plausibly an unintentional vendor bug); a product decision is needed on which discovered quirks to intentionally preserve for compatibility vs. fix.
subsystems.missing_fact: no systematic audit of AutoPilot error/failure behavior exists (malformed-packet handling beyond the specific traced commands, flash-write-failure/power-loss-mid-save behavior, motor stall/fault detection if any)

gap_resolution_a_note: AutoPilot Gap Resolution A (this session) closed all four CONCRETE-type gaps via two bounded concrete-execution scenarios added to tools/unicorn/virtual_link.py: `plus-interactive` (interactive '+' path, mode=0x00) and `manual-f0e0` (0xE0 field layout + dead-man/timeout). Both reuse the existing ConcreteMachine/virtual_link infrastructure and the same AUTOPILOT_RX_ENTRY direct-dispatch boundary every other command scenario in that module already uses; no new analysis framework was added. See docs/replacement/autopilot-gap-audit.md's 'Gap Resolution A' section for the full narrative.
